'''Victoria Jiménez Kasintseva''' (born 9 August 2005) is an Andorran professional [[tennis]] player. On 16 March 2026, she reached a career-high singles ranking by the [[Women's Tennis Association|WTA]] of 89, the first Andorran player, female or male, to break into the top 100 in the tennis rankings in the [[History of tennis|Open Era]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 March 2026 |title=Rankings Watch: Jimenez Kasintseva makes Andorran history; Bucsa vaults spots|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4460733/rankings-watch-bucsas-32-place-leap-jimenez-kasintsevas-andorran-record |access-date=2 March 2026 |website=WTA Tour |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and background==
Victoria Jiménez Kasintseva was born in [[Andorra la Vella]],<ref>[https://www.donasecret.com/personatge-del-mes/vicky-jimenez-princesa-del-roland-garros/ Vicky Jiménez, princesa del Roland Garros]</ref> Andorra to Andorran father Joan Jiménez Guerra and Russian mother Yulia Kasintseva.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Albarrán |first1=Nacho |title=Víctoria Jiménez, andorrana de 14 años, gana el torneo júnior: "Nadal es mi favorito de todos" |url=https://as.com/tenis/2020/02/01/open_australia/1580537835_903431.html |website=Diario AS |access-date=25 April 2024 |language=es |date=7 February 2020}}</ref> Her father is a former tennis professional who reached a career-high [[Association of Tennis Professionals|ATP Tour]] ranking of 505.<ref name="SPORT">{{cite web |last1=Boti |first1=David |title=Victoria Jiménez, la andorrana de 14 años que enamora en Melbourne |url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/open-de-australia-2020/victoria-jimenez-andorrana-enamora-melbourne-7830332 |website=SPORT |access-date=25 April 2024 |language=es |date=31 January 2020}}</ref> Her brother, Joan, also plays tennis. She spent three years of her childhood living in Kentucky in the United States from age 4 to age 8.<ref name="Dona Secret">{{cite web |last1=Grau |first1=Mari Carmen |title=Joan i Vicky Jiménez, tàndem guanyador |url=https://www.donasecret.com/entrevistes/joan-vicky-jimenez-guanyador/ |website=Dona Secret |language=ca |date=19 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Gastiaburú |first1=Analucía |title=Victoria Jiménez Kasintseva, de Andorra para el mundo |url=https://settenis.com.ar/victoria-jimenez-kasintseva-de-andorra-para-el-mundo/ |website=Set Tenis |access-date=26 April 2024 |language=es |date=30 December 2021}}</ref>

She began playing tennis at the age of three in 2008,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tan |first1=Gillian |title=Juniors wrap: Jimenez Kasintseva, Mayot earn AO2020 glory |url=https://ausopen.com/articles/news/juniors-wrap-jimenez-kasintseva-mayot-earn-ao2020-glory |website=Australian Open |access-date=25 April 2024 |date=1 February 2020}}</ref> and currently trains in Barcelona with her father.<ref name="SPORT" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ciriza |first1=Alejandro |title=Jiménez Kasintseva, la luz de Andorra |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2020/02/01/actualidad/1580543596_522611.html |website=El País |access-date=25 April 2024 |language=es |date=1 February 2020}}</ref> She speaks Spanish, English, French, and Russian fluently, in addition to her native [[Catalan language|Catalan]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Macpherson |first1=Alex |title=Conoce a Victoria Jiménez Kasintseva, la pionera adolescente de Andorra |url=https://www.wtatennis.com/es/news/2798471/conoce-a-victoria-jim-nez-kasintseva-la-pionera-adolescente-de-andorra |website=Women's Tennis Association |access-date=25 April 2024 |language=es |date=21 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Solsona |first1=Joan |title=Victoria Jiménez Kasintseva hace historia para Andorra: gana el júnior de Australia con 14 años |url=https://www.marca.com/tenis/open-australia/2020/02/01/5e34f72eca47412b5a8b462f.html |website=MARCA |access-date=25 April 2024 |language=es |date=1 February 2020}}</ref>

==Career==
===Juniors===
In 2020, Jiménez Kasintseva won the [[2020 Australian Open – Girls' singles|Australian Open girls' singles]] title as the youngest player in the draw, defeating [[Weronika Baszak]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ryan |first1=Peter |title=A 14-year-old snares junior girls' Australian Open |url=https://www.theage.com.au/sport/tennis/a-14-year-old-snares-junior-girls-australian-open-20200201-p53wua.html |website=The Age |access-date=25 April 2024 |date=1 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Phelan |first1=Jason |title=Andorran teen wins Aust Open girls' title |url=https://www.northweststar.com.au/story/6609186/andorran-teen-wins-aust-open-girls-title/ |website=The North West Star |access-date=25 April 2024 |date=1 February 2020}}</ref> She was the first Andorran to win a junior major title, as well as the youngest player to win a major final since [[Coco Gauff]] at the [[2018 French Open]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=McCarvel |first1=Nick |title=French boys set for final battle as Jimenez Kasintseva makes history |url=https://www.itftennis.com/en/news-and-media/articles/french-boys-set-for-final-battle-as-jimenez-kasintseva-makes-history/ |website=International Tennis Federation |access-date=25 April 2024 |date=31 January 2020}}</ref> She has won eight singles titles on the [[ITF Junior Circuit]] and one doubles title, and she achieved a career-high junior ranking of No. 1 on 9 March 2020.

* Wimbledon: 1R (2021)

===2021: Professional debut===
At the age of 15, Jiménez Kasintseva made her [[WTA Tour]] main-draw debut as a wildcard at the [[2021 Mutua Madrid Open – Women's singles|2021 Madrid Open]]. She was the youngest player and the first from Andorra to compete in a WTA tournament main draw.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Solsona |first1=Joan |title=Victoria Jiménez Kasintseva, una niña de 15 años entre gigantes |url=https://www.marca.com/tenis/mutua-madrid-open/2021/04/30/608bc77e22601dd1658b4586.html |website=MARCA |access-date=25 April 2024 |language=es |date=30 April 2021}}</ref> Jiménez Kasintseva lost to [[Kiki Bertens]] in the first round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/2122391/former-champions-bertens-kvitova-reach-madrid-second-round|title=Former champions Bertens, Kvitova reach Madrid second round|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=26 July 2025}}</ref> She won her first ITF singles title in Aparecida de Goiânia<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sansaloni |first1=David |title=Vicky I de Goiânia |url=https://www.elperiodic.ad/noticia/89296/vicky-i-de-goiania |website=El Periòdic d'Andorra |access-date=25 April 2024 |language=ca |date=15 November 2021}}</ref> and she reached the final in [[ITF World Tennis Tour Maspalomas|Maspalomas]], where she was defeated by [[Arantxa Rus]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Álvarez |first1=Ivan |title=Vicky Jiménez rep elogis després de brillar a Maspalomas |url=https://www.diariandorra.ad/esports/210824/vicky-jimenez-rep-elogis-despres-brillar-maspalomas_91753.html |website=Diari d'Andorra |access-date=26 April 2024 |language=ca |date=24 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Sansaloni |first1=David |title=Jiménez demana pas |url=https://www.elperiodic.ad/noticia/87613/rss |website=El Periòdic d'Andorra |access-date=26 April 2024 |language=ca |date=23 August 2021}}</ref>

===2022–2024: First WTA Tour quarterfinal and WTA 1000 win===
[[File:Jimenez Kasintseva RGQ22 (7) (52129557771).jpg|thumb|right|upright|Jiménez Kasintseva at the [[2022 French Open]]]]
Having gained entry as a lucky loser, Jiménez Kasintseva recorded her first WTA Tour wins at the [[2022 Korea Open – Women's singles|2022 Korea Open]], defeating [[Chloé Paquet]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tennismajors.com/matches/wta/hana-bank-korea-open/chloe-paquet-vs-victoria-jimenez-kasintseva
|title=Chloe Paquet vs Victoria Jimenez Kasintseva|date=8 November 2022 |publisher=Tennis Majors|accessdate=26 July 2025}}</ref> and [[Rebecca Marino]] to become the first Andorran to reach a first Tour quarterfinal<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/videos/2798354/seoul-jimenez-kasintseva-upsets-marino-becomes-first-andorran-in-wta-qf|title=Seoul: Jimenez Kasintseva becomes first Andorran to reach WTA QF|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=26 July 2025}}</ref> She lost to [[Jeļena Ostapenko]] in the quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/videos/2800419/seoul-ostapenko-storms-past-jimenez-kasintseva-into-5th-sf-of-2022|title=Seoul: Ostapenko storms past Jimenez Kasintseva into 5th SF of 2022|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=26 July 2025}}</ref>
She won her second ITF singles title in Loulé as the top seed in the tournament,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sanjuan |first1=Cesc |title=Nou títol per a Vicky Jiménez en el circuit ITF |url=https://www.andorradifusio.ad/esports/nou-titol-vicky-jimenez-circuit-itf |website=Andorra Difusió |access-date=25 April 2024 |language=ca |date=23 October 2022}}</ref> and won her first ITF Circuit doubles title at the [[Torneig Internacional de Tennis Femení Solgironès|Solgironès Open]], partnered with [[Renata Zarazúa]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Get to know Renata Zarazua |url=https://www.itftennis.com/en/news-and-media/articles/get-to-know-renata-zarazua/ |website=International Tennis Federation |access-date=26 April 2024 |date=3 August 2022}}</ref> Jiménez Kasintseva also reached the singles final in [[2022 Bendigo International|Bendigo]], losing to [[Ysaline Bonaventure]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tornos |first1=Bruno |title=Bonaventure deja a Kasintseva con la miel en los labios |url=https://canaltenis.com/kasintseva-final-bendigo/ |website=Canal Tenis |access-date=26 April 2024 |language=es |date=9 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Romero |first1=Joel |title=Vicky Jiménez subcampiona de l'ITF de Bendigo |url=https://www.andorradifusio.ad/esports/vicky-jimenez-subcampiona-itf-bendigo |website=Andorra Difusió |access-date=26 April 2024 |language=ca |date=9 January 2022}}</ref>

In 2023, she received wildcards into the main draw at the [[WTA 1000 tournaments|WTA 1000]] tournaments in [[2023 Miami Open – Women's singles|Miami]] and [[2023 Mutua Madrid Open – Women's singles|Madrid]], losing in the first round at both. That year, she won two W25 titles, at Boca Raton<ref>{{cite web |last1=Basco |first1=Marc |title=Vicky Jiménez guanya el torneig de Boca Raton |url=https://www.diariandorra.ad/esports/230312/vicky-jimenez-guanya-torneig-boca-raton_121053.html |website=Diari d'Andorra |access-date=25 April 2024 |language=ca |date=12 March 2023}}</ref> and Austin.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Álvarez |first1=Ivan |title=Vicky Jiménez guanya a Austin |url=https://www.diariandorra.ad/esports/231120/vicky-jimenez-guanya-austin_132454.html |website=Diari d'Andorra |access-date=25 April 2024 |language=ca |date=20 November 2023}}</ref>

She also received a wildcard into the main draw at the [[2024 Mutua Madrid Open – Women's singles|2024 Madrid Open]], where she defeated [[Zhu Lin (tennis)|Zhu Lin]] in the first round for her first WTA 1000 win,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/videos/3979605/jimenez-kasintseva-bests-zhu-in-madrid-to-notch-first-wta-1000-win|title=Jimenez Kasintseva bests Zhu in Madrid to notch first WTA 1000 wi|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=26 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tennismajors.com/wta-tour-news/madrid-open-jimenez-kasintseva-reaches-second-round-756794.html|title=Madrid Open: Jimenez Kasintseva reaches second round|date=24 April 2024 |publisher=Tennis Majors|accessdate=26 July 2025}}</ref> then lost to [[Jasmine Paolini]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tennismajors.com/wta-tour-news/madrid-open-paolini-moves-into-third-round-757309.html|title=Madrid Open: Paolini races into third round|date=26 April 2024 |publisher=Tennis Majors|accessdate=26 July 2025}}</ref>

===2025–2026: Historic major, top 100, WTA 1000 debuts===
In March 2025, Jiménez Kasintseva finished runner-up at the [[2025 Antalya Challenger 2 – Singles|Antalya Challenger]], losing to [[Olga Danilović]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tennismajors.com/wta-tour-news/megasaray-hotels-open-2-danilovic-brushes-aside-kasintseva-to-lift-the-title-815404.html|title=Megasaray Hotels Open 2: Danilovic brushes aside Kasintseva to lift the title|date=30 March 2025 |publisher=Tennis Majors|accessdate=26 July 2025}}</ref> She also reached the final at the [[2025 Makarska Open – Singles|WTA 125 Makarska Open]] in Croatia, losing to [[Sára Bejlek]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tennismajors.com/wta-tour-news/makarska-open-bejlek-wins-the-final-825119.html|title=Makarska Open: Bejlek wins the final|date=8 June 2025 |publisher=Tennis Majors|accessdate=26 July 2025}}</ref>

In August 2025, Jiménez Kasintseva [[2025 US Open – Women's singles qualifying|qualified]] for the main draw of the [[2025 US Open – Women's singles|US Open]], making her debut appearance in the main draw of a Grand Slam tournament. With her qualification, she became the first Andorran player, male or female, to compete in the main draw of a major.<ref>{{cite news |last=Macpherson |first=Alex |url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4346784/ito-tjen-set-us-open-qualifying-meeting-valentova-jones-advance |title=Tjen, Ito set US Open qualifying meeting; Valentova, Jones advance |date=22 August 2025 |publisher=[[Women's Tennis Association]] |access-date=23 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4348565/us-open-2025s-grand-slam-debuts-tjen-jimenez-kasintseva-pareja-and-more|title=US Open 2025's Grand Slam debuts: Tjen, Jimenez Kasintseva, Pareja and more|date=24 August 2025|publisher=[[Women's Tennis Association]]}}</ref> She lost to [[Maya Joint]] in the first round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/aug/26/australias-maya-joint-holds-her-nerve-to-reach-us-open-second-round|title=Alex de Minaur serves up clinical display while Maya Joint holds her nerve at US Open|publisher=The Guardian|accessdate=28 August 2025}}</ref>

At the [[2026 Mérida Open – Singles|2026 Mérida Open]], she qualified for the main-draw and defeated [[Yulia Putintseva]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/videos/4455930/jimenez-kastintseva-reels-in-putintseva-from-4-2-down-in-decider|title=In Merida, Jimenez Kasintseva reels in Putintseva from 4-2 down in decider|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=7 March 2026}}</ref> and eighth seed [[Magda Linette]] to make it through to the quarterfinals,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/videos/4457351/jimenez-kasintseva-overcomes-linette-in-320-epic-to-make-merida-quarters|title=Jimenez Kasintseva overcomes Linette in 3:20 epic to make Merida quarters|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=7 March 2026}}</ref> at which point her run was ended by fellow qualifier [[Zhang Shuai]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/videos/4459182/zhang-wins-battle-of-the-qualifiers-handles-jimenez-kasintseva-to-reach-merida-semis|title=Zhang wins battle of the qualifiers in Merida, into first WTA 500 semifinal since 2022|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=7 March 2026}}</ref> Despite the loss, Jiménez Kasintseva moved up 25 places in the WTA rankings to No. 97 on 2 March 2026, becoming the first player from Andorra – female or male – to break into the world's top 100.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4460733/rankings-watch-bucsas-32-place-leap-jimenez-kasintsevas-andorran-record|title=Rankings Watch: Bucsa vaults 32 spots, Jimenez Kasintseva makes Andorran history|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=7 March 2026}}</ref> Later that week at the WTA 1000 tournament in [[2026 BNP Paribas Open – Women's singles|Indian Wells]], she again progressed through the qualifying rounds to earn a spot in the main draw and then overcame [[Caty McNally]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/videos/4462355/jimenez-kasintseva-soars-past-mcnally-to-reach-indian-wells-second-round|title=Jimenez Kasintseva soars past McNally to reach Indian Wells second round|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=7 March 2026}}</ref> before losing to 16th seed [[Naomi Osaka]] in the second round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.tennistemple.com/video/osaka-defeats-jimenez-kasintseva-at-indi/n7ytQ|title=Osaka defeats Jimenez Kasintseva at Indian Wells 2026 – Round 2|publisher=Tennis Temple|accessdate=7 March 2026}}</ref>
